question: to the Commission Aodhán Ó Ríordáin (S&D) Subject:
Interim EUR 3 flat-rate customs duty applied to printed books and magazines

From 1 July 2026, an interim flat-rate customs duty of EUR 3 per declaration line applies to low-value e-commerce consignments entering the EU, under Council Regulation (EU) 2026/382 of 11 February 20261, as implemented by Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1200 of 5 June 20262. This measure targets fast fashion and non-compliant goods, not culture and education. Printed books (CN/TARIC 4901 99 00) carry a 0 % most-favoured nation (MFN) customs duty, reflecting the EU’s commitment to safeguarding literature and academic material. However, Article 2 of Council Regulation (EU) 2026/382 applies the EUR 3 duty to all qualifying consignments regardless of tariff classification, with no exemption for books. A book is charged the same EUR 3 duty as any other item, irrespective of heading. In Ireland, constituents report that book shipments via An Post’s clearance portal, correctly identified as ‘books’, are still charged the EUR 3 duty plus a EUR 6.95 handling fee. 1.
Was the Commission aware, when implementing Council Regulation (EU) 2026/382, that it would apply uniformly to books otherwise carrying 0 % MFN duty?
Does the Commission consider it compatible with the EU’s cultural and educational objectives for this duty to apply indiscriminately to books?
Will the Commission bring forward a carve-out for CN 4901 goods, or clarify how one can be introduced before the measure ends on 1 July 2028?

OJ L, 2026/382, 18.2.2026, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/382/oj (http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/382/oj). 2 OJ L, 2026/1200, 8.6.2026, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg_impl/2026/1200/oj (http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg_impl/2026/1200/oj). 1
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (8.9.2026) Council Regulation (EU) 2026/3821 abolishes the EUR 150 threshold-based customs duty exemption and imposes, from 1 July 2026 until 1 July 2028, a temporary EUR 3 customs duty per item in consignments valued at up to EUR 150 and sold in distance sales. This in principle includes books and magazines. However, imported goods can benefit from existing duty exemptions or preferential treatment if they fulfil the relevant conditions. Books and magazines printed in third countries and meeting the rules of origin with those third countries for which the EU has preferential trade agreements can benefit from preferential duty rates, if the appropriate proof of origin is provided when required to customs. If the preferential treatment applies, it must be claimed by declaring the goods using a normal (H1) customs declaration. The simplified (H7) declaration cannot be used for preferential treatment, as it does not contain the data elements necessary to claim preferential origin. Pursuant to the Duty Relief Regulation2, the duty-free import of certain educational, scientific and cultural materials will still be possible, provided that certain conditions are met. For example, it will be possible to import duty-free microfilms of books, children’s picture books or colouring books, maps, scientific charts and diagrams, if the advertising contained therein does not cover more than 25 % of the surface. The Commission will, by 1 October 2026, assess the impact of the temporary EUR 3 customs duty on possible diversions of trade flows and unintended consequences for specific categories of goods, such as books and magazines. If appropriate, the Commission will consider submitting a proposal to amend Council Regulation (EU) 2026/382.
